lesson_title: Same R200 a Month. Six Times the Money.
hook_text: Two friends save the same R200 a month. One ends up with about six times more. Here's the secret.
clip_script: Lebo starts saving R200 a month at twenty. Sam starts at forty. Same amount, same eight percent growth. At sixty, Lebo has roughly six times what Sam has. Why? Compound interest: your interest earns interest, and it snowballs over time. Sam missed twenty years of snowballing. So: safe jar first, a savings account or stokvel for emergencies. Then a growth jar for the long term: unit trusts, shares, a retirement fund. Higher returns mean higher risk, so spread it out. And that WhatsApp message promising five times your money next month? Scam. Start early, start small, and let time work for you.
visual_style: A whiteboard graph with two savings curves, one starting at 20 and one at 40, and a snowball rolling down a hill growing bigger.
pacing: A quick setup, a slow reveal of the two curves, then rapid-fire tips.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set one savings goal you can start this month.
